text: Delivered as an ASCII diagram in a fenced code block that shows components and a numbered flow for send, fan-out and reconnect, followed by short notes.

The sender is acked only after the Message Store commit, and the ack carries the message id and per-conversation sequence number. A failed write returns an error with no fan-out, and a retry with the same client-generated id does not create a duplicate.
Fan-out runs off the sender's request path, and is guaranteed for every acknowledged message even if a process crashes right after the write.
Presence is based on 10 s heartbeats, with users treated as offline after 30 s without one. Live delivery uses a client ack, and a 5 s timeout falls back to offline handling.
Offline recipients have their missed messages kept for up to 30 days and get a best-effort push notification: no retries, and no effect on storage.
On reconnect the client receives all missed messages in per-conversation sequence order. Delivery is at-least-once, and clients drop duplicates by message id.
The notes say where each piece of state lives and what happens on each failure.
